messages:
Ellen (sales): Heads up — ZenithHealth POC failing on Friday demos. Their QA sees sporadic TLS failures to our private endpoint from one AZ only. Can infra/devops swarm? :ambulance:

Zenith-Network: From eu-west-1a we see connection resets during TLS handshake. eu-west-1b is fine. No 5xx on your side. Sample curl from failing host:

Zenith-Network: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-zenith.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private.redwood-zenith.internal/health
*   Trying 10.3.44.22...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to private.redwood-zenith.internal (10.3.44.22) port 443 (#0)
* OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to private.redwood-zenith.internal:443
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to private.redwood-zenith.internal:443```

Marcus (infra): Can you paste a tcpdump or packet log from the failing host? This smells like PMTU/fragmentation or middlebox dropping large TLS ClientHello.

Zenith-Network: Here's a short tcpdump around the handshake. Notice the ICMP "frag needed":

Zenith-Network: ```12:03:14.123456 IP 10.5.2.10.52344 > 10.3.44.22.443: Flags [S], seq 123456, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
12:03:14.123789 IP 10.3.44.22.443 > 10.5.2.10.52344: Flags [S.], seq 654321, ack 123457, win 28960, options [mss 1460], length 0
12:03:14.124000 IP 10.5.2.10.52344 > 10.3.44.22.443: Flags [P.], seq 123457:123910, ack 654322, win 6376, length 453
12:03:14.124200 IP 198.51.100.200 > 10.5.2.10: ICMP 3/4 frag needed and DF set (mtu 1400)
12:03:14.124450 IP 10.5.2.10.52344 > 10.3.44.22.443: Flags [R], seq 123910, win 0, length 0```

Tess (solutions): That ICMP frag-needed with mtu 1400 indicates a path MTU black hole — intermediate appliance is telling the sender to fragment but DF is set and then it resets. Some egress devices block ICMP or don't pass it back, causing larger TLS ClientHello packets to be dropped. We've seen TLS client hello sizes > 400 bytes when cert chains/OCSP/stapling are present.

Ravi (eng-ml): Our client hello is around 512-900 bytes depending on ciphers and extensions. We recently enabled a cert with long chain and OCSP stapling; that increases size. Could explain AZ-specific behavior if a firewall in that AZ is misconfigured.

Marcus (infra): Options: a) Customer allows ICMP type 3 code 4 through (fixes PMTU), b) we ask them to clamp MSS on their egress appliance to 1400 or 1360, c) we reduce ClientHello size (disable stapling, remove some extensions) for a POC build, d) route that AZ's traffic via the working AZ/peering bypass. Which is feasible short-term for demo?

Zenith-Network: Security is reluctant to open ICMP widely. Clamping MSS on the egress appliance for traffic to your 203.0.113.0/24 seems acceptable for a 48-hour window. They can apply an outbound policy to set MSS=1400 for that prefix.

Tess (solutions): For the POC we can also offer a small config change on our side: terminate TLS at an ALB with a cert with a slimmer chain and temporarily disable OCSP stapling to shrink ClientHello slightly. That reduces blast radius if they can't change MSS quickly.

Marcus (infra): Action plan: 1) @Zenith-Network apply MSS clamp 1400 for destination 203.0.113.77/32 for 48 hours. 2) @Ravi we will provision an alternate ALB offering with stapling disabled and TLS1.2-only as fallback. 3) Monitor logs. If MSS clamp works, we'll revert ALB changes.

network-bot: policy-notice: detected potential ICMP-block on zenith-egress-appliance-1 (198.51.100.200). Recommend MSS clamp or ICMP allow for full fix.

Zenith-Network: We can apply MSS clamp for the window. ETA 45m to deploy and test. Who should we ping once it's live?

Ellen (sales): Ping this thread and DM me the security sign-off details. We'll confirm with Zenith security as well.

Ravi (eng-ml): I'll stand up the fallback ALB config in parallel. deploy-bot: queueing task create-poc-alb(203.0.113.77, tls-fallback) -> status: queued

Marcus (infra): After MSS clamp goes live, run the same curl and tcpdump. If we still see resets we'll switch traffic to the fallback ALB.

Zenith-Network: MSS clamp rolled out. Test output from the same host:

Zenith-Network: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-zenith.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private.redwood-zenith.internal/health
*   Trying 203.0.113.77...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 203.0.113.77 (203.0.113.77) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS 1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: private.redwood-zenith.internal
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "status": "ok" }
* Connection #0 to host 203.0.113.77 left intact
```

Tess (solutions): Great — looks like MSS clamp fixed it. We'll keep monitoring for 24 hours and then remove the clamp after the demo window unless you want a long-term fix. For long-term we recommend either enabling ICMP PMTU or a persistent MSS clamp and documenting it in the onboarding guide.

Zenith-Network: Security happy to keep it for 72h then revert. We'll send the ACL/rollback ticket to your contact.

Ellen (sales): Thanks all — documented. Closing the swarm unless new issues pop up. :tada:
